title: Keep teaching and its check apart
statement: Keep a worked example and the independent check of the same idea on different screens, and fail any option sharing five or more consecutive words with on-screen teaching text.
detail: The reading course's authoring playbook, written so that the 16 mistakes of a first lesson build are prevented at authoring time, says the teaching display (example and non-example) and the independent check may not share a screen, so the check needs a reread of the passage and no option is near-verbatim to the example. Its self-audit checklist fails any check answerable by visible word-match, a run of five or more words shared by an option and the same screen's teaching text. A read of a demonstration unit as delivered found its teaching articles had pre-answered their certified release checks, a must-fix.
against: Two approved reference lessons check a just-taught idea on the same page, and an adjudication ruled that teaching-then-checking on one page is the pattern, not a leak (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-course/G3-U1-L4-RESIDUAL-ADJUDICATION-2026-08-21.md`, line 35); the five-word threshold is one playbook's choice.

evidence.quote: The teaching display (example/nonexample) and the independent check may not share a screen
word overlap between an option and same-screen teaching text = fail).
Gradual-release leak: l0/l1 teaching articles pre-answered their certified release checks (must-fix)

The modelling page holds ONLY the passage and the think-aloud (plus the think-aloud's own optional `why_check`). Never put an `scr`, `msq` or other child-answered item on a modelling page: the whole point of "I do" is that the guide does it, and a gated question here reverses the release.

On L4 every word of the correct option appears in the sentence just spoken (100%); on L5, L6 and L7 the overlap is 44-55%, which is ordinary. A non-responding child can clear a required gate by echoing.
so the "independent" check is answerable purely by matching visible words from two paragraphs above it, never by rereading the passage.
